---
title: "Contribute"
description: "How to propose a workflow, a prompt, a skill or any other contribution."
---

Anyone can propose a contribution with a short form on GitHub (a free GitHub account is needed). Pick what you want to share:

::: {.form-buttons}
[Workflow](https://github.com/astronomicalintelligence/site/issues/new?template=1-workflow.yml){.form-button .type-workflows}
[Prompt](https://github.com/astronomicalintelligence/site/issues/new?template=2-prompt.yml){.form-button .type-prompts}
[Skill](https://github.com/astronomicalintelligence/site/issues/new?template=3-skill.yml){.form-button .type-skills}
[Agent config](https://github.com/astronomicalintelligence/site/issues/new?template=4-agent-config.yml){.form-button .type-agent-configs}
[Model check](https://github.com/astronomicalintelligence/site/issues/new?template=5-model-check.yml){.form-button .type-model-checks}
[Paper to review](https://github.com/astronomicalintelligence/site/issues/new?template=6-review.yml){.form-button .type-reviews}
[Failure](https://github.com/astronomicalintelligence/site/issues/new?template=7-failure.yml){.form-button .type-failures}
:::

Each form needs three or four answers, which takes a few minutes. You are credited with the name on your GitHub profile unless you list other authors. You can drag and drop images (screenshots, plots) into any text box. Use only images you made or may share under CC BY 4.0.

A maintainer reads every proposal. If something is missing, the issue gets the label **needs-info** and a comment that says what: edit the issue to add it. When it is complete it becomes a page.

## What each form asks for

The fields in **bold** are required.

- Workflow: **what it does**, **the steps** with the prompts exactly as used, **how to check the result**.
- Prompt: **what it does**, **the prompt** exactly as used, **how to check the result**, a real example.
- Skill: **what it does**, `SKILL.md` (pasted, or a .zip of the skill folder), **how to check the result**.
- Agent config: **what it does and for which projects**, **the whole `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`**, **how to check the result**.
- Model check: **what it checks**, **the prompt**, **the expected answer with the rule to mark a reply pass or fail**, the results for each model you tried.
- Paper to review: **the published paper**, **whether it is open access**, **why it is worth a second review**, **whether you could check the model's points**. Reviews follow the [ground rules](reviews/index.qmd#ground-rules).
- Failure: **what happened** (model, date, what it answered and what was right), **how to catch or avoid it**.

Workflows, prompts, skills and agent configs can also say **how you tested it**: the model, the date and the real case you ran it on. A tested contribution is published as **L1**; an untested one as an **L0** draft. All of them can list **known failures** and a research phase.

## Catalogue numbers

When a contribution is published it gets a catalogue number: the letter of its type and a number, for example **AI W0003** for a workflow or **AI P0002** for a prompt. The number never changes and is part of the page's address, so you can use it to cite or mention the contribution.

## Credit and citation

Every contributed page shows its authors and ends with a **How to cite** box. Each page also keeps a **History** of its versions.

Contributions are published under the site licences: text under CC BY 4.0, code under MIT.

## Review criteria

- A colleague in the same field can follow the contribution and reuse it.
- Prompts are given exactly as used.
- Nothing confidential or under embargo is included.

A contribution enters at **L1** when the author has tested it on a real case. It moves to **L2** when someone else reproduces it. Untested contributions are welcome too: they are published as **L0** drafts.

## Updating a contribution

A contribution keeps its catalogue number for life. Use **Suggest an update**, at the bottom of its page, when:

- you tested it again, with another model or on another date;
- you fixed or clarified a step, or improved a prompt;
- you found a new failure;
- you reproduced it (L1 to L2) or checked it across models (L3).

If you used it and it went wrong, use **It failed for me** on the same page. The update goes through the same review, and the page records it in its History. Whoever rewrites a substantial part of a contribution is added to its authors; smaller changes, reproduction (L1->L2) are credited in the History. When you cite a contribution that has been updated, give the date of the version you used: the catalogue number and the address stay the same.

If the method itself changes, propose a new contribution instead. It gets a new number and says *Supersedes AI W0002* at the top, and the old page links to it.
